items.summary: On a blistering afternoon in June, when the temperature had crossed 40 degrees Celsius, 48-year-old Manju (name changed on request) was at home in the dense Mewla Maharajpur locality. She wanted a few minutes of rest before heading out to work as a domestic worker. But the ceiling fan in the room, recirculating hot air, was not helping her cool down. Dreading the blazing sun, Manju reminded herself that it was only a 20-minute-walk to her employer’s home, and that she had been doing this for decades. A few minutes into the walk, she knew something was terribly wrong. “I began to feel overwhelming thirst, followed by a parched throat and nausea. I sat on the side of the road and managed to get drinking water from someone nearby,” she said. Manju’s symptoms indicate that she may have experienced heat exhaustion that arises due to the body's response to an excessive loss of water and salt, usually through profuse sweating. items.summary: Supreme Court Justice Ujjal Bhuyan on Saturday said that scientific temper lays the foundation for the rule of law, since arbitrary power feeds on a society that does not question. A society that stops asking questions becomes vulnerable to authoritarianism, he emphasised. "I believe, scientific temperament lays the foundation for the rule of law. This is because arbitrary power thrives on ignorance, fear and unexamined belief," he said. Thus, a society which believes tradition should be immune from scrutiny will fail to reform unjust practices, he opined. "A society that accepts claims without evidence is susceptible to superstitious beliefs and becomes vulnerable to mis-information. A society that fears questions becomes vulnerable to authoritarianism. A society that treats tradition as beyond scrutiny may fail to reform unjust practices," he said. Justice Bhuyan was delivering the address at the 12th convocation ceremony of the University of Science and Technology Meghalaya (USTM). The Commissioner said Ritesh Pandey, who was arrested in Delhi on October 24, told investigators that he and Vinod Sharma bought the phone from a shop in Karol Bagh on the instructions of Prajwal Prasad. This is as per Pandey’s statement. Both Prasad and Sharma are absconding and have moved anticipatory bail petitions,” Seemant said.
